interpretations.text: Proposed LP reading, not platform format: tracks 1–5 form Side A (14:03), tracks 6–9 Side B (12:47). Total 26:50 is arithmetic on displayed times, not measured playback.
Tracks 1–2 establish a still domestic morning and an intimate second-person address; 'home' is presented as shared presence rather than property or location.
Track 3 changes the premise from receiving light to making color together. Gray, mud and rain persist; the protagonists choose how to meet them.
Track 4 travels through pines, creek and porch traces; repeated finding becomes the lyric's return mechanism. This is a reading of text, not literal biography.
Track 5 is the shortest at 1:52 and functions as a plausible side hinge: needle dust, tape hiss, flute, bass and underground currents replace the explicit search narrative.
Track 6 converts that underground/current vocabulary into open water, surf and the return to 'you'; Side B begins in motion rather than arrival.
Tracks 7–8 enlarge the scale from a makeshift home to blooming and sunlight; their repeated 'we' frames joy as something made with another person.
Track 9 deliberately ends in a messy kitchen, jam and toastbread rather than triumph. 'don't fix the moment' (lyric) suggests allowing imperfect intimacy to remain.
The album opens at waking and closes at going to bed: a suggested day-shaped loop, though no creator-stated concept or technical track ancestry was verified.

Recurring words and objects include blue, bloom, hands, home, pines, water, rain, light, kettles, bread, rooms and 'you'. Cross-track motif resemblance is not evidence of intended narrative causality.
Public song-page style labels shift from folk/bedroom pop toward psychedelic country-electronica, jazz/boom-bap and grunge/phonk, then pop. This is a metadata comparison, not an audition of sound.
One song remains a source artifact; the nine-track order is an album-level composition. This proposal describes the reading of that order, not an authoritative or released side division.
